caption: The drawing depicts a pair of closed wooden window shutters mounted within a rectangular window frame. The shutters are painted a weathered blue-green color, with areas of wood grain and brownish discoloration visible throughout, indicating age and exposure. Each shutter features a symmetrical geometric cutout or inlay, resembling an hourglass shape, outlined by shallow grooves. The shutters are joined in the center by a thin vertical gap, and a small, unobtrusive latch or handle is present where the panels meet. Four metal hinges, rusted and brown, are attached at the upper and lower corners of each shutter, securing them to the stone or plaster wall suggested by irregular grayish shading around the window. The background is a plain, light beige color, with some faint pencil lines and the artist's signature, "Bertha Semple," appearing below the window.
title: Cabinet Doors at Mission San Jose de Guadalupe
cluster: #12 — Spanish Colonial Art of the Southwest
